# Overview

The purpose of this document is to compare how many and which samples have valid nicotine metabolism ratio (NMR) values based on different methods of creating standard curves for back calculation of sample concentrations of nicotine metabolite data generated by LC/MS/MS.
The original method done was based on modified R scripts from collaborators at the University of Washington. The methods tested here use a tool called SCALiR that was converted from a streamlit app to a command-line interface tool. This tool has three potential options for fitting standard curve models including 'fixed', 'interval', and 'wide'. Here we compare the original and all SCALiR model fit methods to determine which model fit is able to provide the highest number of samples with concentrations within the range of quantitation.

Read in data:
```{r}
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

og_results <- fread("data/SHSph2_NMRwSurveyDF_clean20240729CRM.csv")
scalir_fixed <- fread("results/fixed/valid_filtered_samples_nmr.csv")
scalir_interval <- fread("results/interval/valid_filtered_samples_nmr.csv")
scalir_wide <- fread("results/wide/valid_filtered_samples_nmr.csv")
combined_results <- fread("results/combined/valid_filtered_samples_nmr.csv")
```

Wrangle results data:
```{r}
# Function for changing the sample ID column to character values and dropping all NA's in the logNMR column
wrangle_results <- function(df, id_col, nmr_col){
  df <- df %>% mutate(across(all_of(id_col), as.character)) %>% drop_na(nmr_col)
  return(df)
}
# Use function on OG results
og_results <- wrangle_results(og_results, 'idNo', 'logNMR')
# Create a list of the SCALiR results
scalir_results <- list(scalir_fixed, scalir_interval, scalir_wide)
# Set the names for the dataframes in the list
names(scalir_results) <- c("scalir_fixed", "scalir_interval", "scalir_wide")
# Loop over the dataframes in the list with the wrangle_results function
scalir_results <- lapply(scalir_results, wrangle_results, id_col = 'sample_id', nmr_col = 'logNMR')
# Move the items from the list back to the global environment
list2env(scalir_results, env=globalenv())

```

Create list of sample IDs for each of the results:
```{r}
valid_samples <- list(
        original = og_results$idNo,
        scalir_fixed = scalir_fixed$sample_id,
        scalir_interval = scalir_interval$sample_id,
        scalir_wide = scalir_wide$sample_id
)
```
Make Venn diagrams of the valid samples
```{r}
library(ggvenn)
ggvenn(valid_samples,
       fill_color = c("#0073C2FF", "#EFC000FF", "#868686FF", "#CD534CFF"),
       stroke_size = 0.5,
       set_name_size = 4)

ggvenn(valid_samples[2:4],
       fill_color = c("#EFC000FF", "#868686FF", "#CD534CFF"),
       stroke_size = 0.5,
       set_name_size = 4)

ggvenn(valid_samples[1:2],
       fill_color = c("#0073C2FF", "#EFC000FF"),
       stroke_size = 0.5,
       set_name_size = 4)

ggvenn(valid_samples[c(1,3)],
       fill_color = c("#0073C2FF", "#868686FF"),
       stroke_size = 0.5,
       set_name_size = 4)

ggvenn(valid_samples[c(1,4)],
       fill_color = c("#0073C2FF", "#CD534CFF"),
       stroke_size = 0.5,
       set_name_size = 4)
```

Evaluate the set differences:
```{r}
# Unique SCALiR fixed
fixed_unique <- setdiff(scalir_fixed$sample_id, scalir_interval$sample_id)
scalir_fixed[scalir_fixed$sample_id %in% fixed_unique,]

# Unique SCALiR wide
wide_unique <- setdiff(scalir_wide$sample_id, scalir_interval$sample_id)
scalir_wide[scalir_wide$sample_id %in% wide_unique,]

# Unique interval
interval_unique <- setdiff(scalir_interval$sample_id, og_results$idNo)
interval_unique_df <- scalir_interval[scalir_interval$sample_id %in% interval_unique,]
hist(interval_unique_df$logNMR)

# Unique original
og_unique <- setdiff(og_results$idNo, c(scalir_interval$sample_id, scalir_wide$sample_id))
og_unique_df <- og_results[og_results$idNo %in% og_unique,]
hist(og_unique_df$logNMR)

```
